5NFkC0umAKe8An9SflzrCn.title: Today Won’t Come Again

s.t: Kanye West built ‘Hey Mama’ on a sample of Donal Leace's 1972 song, and Leace is credited as a songwriter on it.
s.q: is based around a sample of the 1972 track "Today Won't Come Again", as written and performed by American musician Donal Leace

s.t: Donal Leace recorded it in New York in 1971 with Keith Jarrett on piano and Roberta Flack singing backing vocals, on sessions where Eumir Deodato arranged the horns and strings.
s.q: Keith Jarrett (piano), David Spinozza (guitar), Bill Salter (bass), Bill LaVorgna (drums), Donal Leace (vocal, guitar), Roberta Flack (background vocal on track 1) ... Today Won't Come Again; Eumir Deodato (arranger)

f.t: He recorded At The Shadows at The Shadows restaurant in Washington in 1962 with Carol Hedin, a white autoharpist, in a groundbreaking racial crossover.
f.q: His 1962 recording "At The Shadows" with Carol Hedin was groundbreaking featuring Leace, a black male folk singer-guitarist and Hedin, a white female singer and autoharpist, a racial crossover.

f.t: He worked and lived at The Cellar Door in Georgetown, and the club once displayed a sign reading “The Home of Donal Leace”.
f.q: During the 1960s, he worked and lived at The Cellar Door in Georgetown.  For a while a sign at the club read “The Home of Donal Leace”.

f.t: He chaired the theatre department at Washington's Duke Ellington School of the Arts, where he mentored students including Dave Chappelle and the opera singer Denyce Graves.
f.q: Leace mentored students, including Chappelle and acclaimed opera singer Denyce Graves.

f.t: He first performed professionally at Carnegie Chapter Hall in New York in 1959, then based himself in Washington and became known as “Washington's Favorite Folk Singer”.
f.q: Donal made his first professional folk singing appearance at Carnegie Chapter Hall, in New York City, 1959.
